statements.markdown:
The second formal statement has three clauses. Given a minimizer and an
associated diffusion, it establishes convergence of the finite-spin
ground-state values, a bounded martingale with a spin-valued terminal
limit, convergence of the gradient and the value identities. Under the
same hypotheses and fixed $0<T<1$, it gives eventual positivity of the
Gaussian normalizers and convergence of the finite coefficient sum.

statements.markdown:
Following it generates the state

$$
X_t=B_t+\int_0^t\gamma(s)u(s,X_s)\,ds,\qquad X_0=0.
$$

This is the **associated diffusion**, whose existence and uniqueness for
a fixed Brownian motion follow from the cited regularity theorem.

lean.clause: gradient W γ s (X (Real.toNNReal s) ω))
lean.name: OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.IsDiffusion
lean.note: Support model. The drift at time s depends only on s and the state at s.
lean.plain: X is a diffusion for γ

statements.markdown:
We first fix $\gamma$ and obtain the deterministic value and slope by
optimising the expected future payoff. We then use that slope as a rule
along a random path. Computing an expected future payoff reveals nothing
about the future noise, and at time $t$ the rule needs only $t$ and the
state already reached.

reached state.
